$comment: Typed-statement predicate enum — spec/SPEC.md §21. CLOSED and VERSIONED: a predicate not listed here is rejected by five_d_nd.statement.statement_violations(), never silently classified by keyword guessing (that is an nD grammar's own binding concern, §9 — this vocabulary is 5D's OWN closed list for the typed-statement layer). Every predicate maps to EXACTLY ONE of the five dimensions (§2); the mapping itself is part of this document's own digest (via grounding.digest over this file's canonical JSON), so a predicate's dimension assignment is pinned, not re-derived per caller. MODAL FORCE (an obligation, a permission, a prohibition) IS NEVER A STATEMENT PREDICATE: O/P/F are nD deontic claims (§7, §9's co-dimension), never a 5D predicate here — a predicate below names a FACT or an ACT, never the deontic force that may separately attach to it.

is_a.definition: A legal/legislative definition: the subject span IS the thing the object span defines ('X' means ...). Structural because a definition fixes what a term IS MADE OF / IS AN INSTANCE OF — containment of meaning, not causation or purpose.

part_of.definition: The subject is a structural component, or named sub-unit, of the object (a filing system, a group of undertakings, a listed measure within a broader set of measures). Direction is ALWAYS part-to-whole (the smaller unit is subj, the larger unit is obj) — a clause surfacing the SAME relation whole-first ('X includes Y') is coded with subj and obj SWAPPED, never as a second predicate. 'part of' is NOT a determiner to strip from a subj/obj span: 'part of X' names a distinct entity (a component or portion of X), kept WHOLE in its own span; where the text relates that component to a SEPARATE named whole by a GENUINE containment relation ('X forms part of Y'), it is coded as a part_of Statement, subj the component, obj the whole — never silently collapsed by treating 'part of' as equivalent to 'a'/'the'. 'form(s) part of' is a part_of VERB CUE in its own right ('X form(s) part of Y'), the same way 'unless'/'except' are except_when cues. 'References to X include Y' is a DIFFERENT pattern: an INTERPRETIVE/DEFINITIONAL extension clause that stipulates the TERM X, wherever referenced, is to be READ as covering Y too -- Y FALLS WITHIN THE SCOPE of the term X, coded applies_to, NEVER is_a, NEVER part_of, even where Y is also, physically, a part of X's own referent.

applies_to.definition: A scope provision: the subject instrument's own applicability is fixed onto the object (a kind of processing, a category of actor, a territory), INCLUDING a concessive clause that keeps the rule in force despite a named FACT OR CIRCUMSTANCE ('notwithstanding the fact that...', 'irrespective of whether...'). Routing test for notwithstanding/irrespective of/subject to: route to except_when ONLY when the object's own HEAD NOUN is itself a provision reference (paragraph, Article, section, subsection, point, subparagraph, or a named act: 'notwithstanding paragraph 2', 'notwithstanding Article 5', 'subject to subsection (2)'); a thing merely QUALIFIED by 'referred to in...' or 'pursuant to...' does not count ('the terms of the arrangement referred to in paragraph 1' has head noun 'terms', not 'paragraph' -- paragraph 1 is identified, not set aside) and stays applies_to, concessive; 'subject to [a condition or requirement]' (head noun is not a provision reference, e.g. 'appropriate safeguards') is requires, not applies_to or except_when -- the condition is something the act must satisfy, not a provision setting the rule aside. A savings clause ('without prejudice to X', 'shall not affect X') is neither this nor except_when -- it is cross_references, a non-overriding link from the host provision to X, with negation: "absent" (the 'not' is part of the savings cue, never a negator) unless a separate negator applies. 'References to X include Y' is ALSO this predicate: Y FALLS WITHIN THE SCOPE of the TERM X, wherever X is referenced elsewhere in the instrument -- never is_a (not a fresh definition of a new term), and never part_of (even where Y is physically a part of X's own referent); see part_of's own definition, above.

cross_references.definition: A citation from one provision to another ('referred to in Article N'), INCLUDING a savings clause ('without prejudice to X', 'shall not affect X', 'is without prejudice to X') -- a non-overriding link from the host provision to X, never a derogation (except_when) and never a negated scope claim (applies_to with negation present); the clause's own 'not', when present ('shall not affect X'), is part of the savings cue itself, never a negator -- negation: "absent" unless a separate negator applies. A fact about the citing sentence's own surface form, never itself normative (§7 N1 is unaffected).

except_when.definition: A TRUE exception or derogation: the subject's own general rule does NOT apply under the stated condition named by the object. Cues are restricted to a closed set that actually expresses non-application -- 'unless', 'except', 'by way of derogation from', 'save where' -- PLUS 'notwithstanding'/'irrespective of'/'subject to' ONLY WHEN their own object's HEAD NOUN is itself a provision reference (a paragraph, Article, section, subsection, point, subparagraph, or named act -- see applies_to's own routing test; a thing merely qualified by 'referred to in...' does not count, and 'subject to [a condition]' with a non-provision head noun is requires, not this). 'X does not apply to Y' is except_when only when Y is a scope CARVE-OUT stated as part of defining the rule's own boundary; otherwise it is applies_to with negation: "present". A savings clause is neither this nor applies_to -- see cross_references.

enables.definition: The subject makes the object POSSIBLE or PRODUCES it as a mechanism — a precondition/capability/production relation, with no stated purpose and no deontic modal of its own. Causal: 'enables' is one of the originals' own causal-gloss verbs ('triggers, enables, prevents').

requires.definition: A trigger/condition relation: when the subject's own antecedent fires (a breach, a high-risk processing type, or 'subject to [a condition or requirement]' whose own head noun is not a provision reference), the object ACT follows as its consequence. The object is the ACT ITSELF, NEVER framed as 'an obligation' or any other deontic wrapper; whether the act is ALSO owed as a deontic duty is separate, nD knowledge this predicate does not encode. No MODAL verb (shall/may/must/should/'is to be'/'shall be deemed'/'shall be held') is ever inside the object span either -- strip the modal, keep only the residual act. A negator inside the ANTECEDENT ('cannot', 'unable', 'no') stays INSIDE the subj span, as part of what the antecedent SAYS -- under §21, negation: "present" means the RELATION ITSELF is negated, which a negator confined to the antecedent's own content never does; such a Statement is negation: "absent". The companion deadline_of Statement for a period N named in the consequence is ALSO negation: "absent", for the identical reason (see deadline_of's own definition).

legislative_purpose_of.definition: A recital-position purpose statement: the subject (an instrument, a provision) IS INTENDED TO / AIMS TO bring about the object, stated descriptively, with NO deontic modal of its own.

compliance_purpose_of.definition: An operative-article purpose clause carrying a modal ('shall ... for the purpose of ...'): the subject act is undertaken FOR the stated object, inside a binding obligation.

based_on.definition: LEGAL BASIS ONLY: the object names the legal ground that JUSTIFIES the subject act or provision ('is based on the data subject's explicit consent', 'based on Article 6(1)'). Intentional, not causal: the originals' own intentional gloss is 'goals, justification, telos', and a legal basis is a JUSTIFICATION offered for an act, not a mechanical cause of it — nothing about naming a legal ground MAKES the act happen in the way a trigger does. Also not structural: a legal basis is not a containment or scope relation; the instrument's own provision may itself be CITED as the ground (cross_references already covers the citation itself), but based_on names the JUSTIFICATION role that citation plays, not the citation. A clause describing HOW a decision is PRODUCED (a mechanism — 'a decision based solely on automated processing') is enables, never based_on: the mechanism/means question is causal, the justification question is intentional, and surface 'based on' wording alone does not decide which. A 'Where X is based on Y, [modal] Z' trigger/consequence clause is requires, never based_on, even though the words 'based on' appear inside it.

precedes.definition: An explicit ordering relation: the subject event/act happens BEFORE the object event/act ('prior to', 'before').

deadline_of.definition: A bounded-duration relation: the object names a fixed time window or deadline within which the subject act must occur. Distinguished from requires (the TRIGGER itself) and from precedes (bare ordering, no duration). A negator about meeting this deadline ('where/if ... cannot be achieved ... within N') stays INSIDE the antecedent of the SEPARATE requires Statement it is part of (see requires's own definition); it does not negate the RELATION of either Statement, so THIS Statement, naming N itself, stays negation: "absent" -- the same as its own companion requires Statement.

predication.definition: The DEFAULT predicate (§2, §3): an ordinary copula or modal assertion ('X is Y', 'the controller shall ensure that...') that does not fall under any of the other fourteen predicates. A PURE modal clause with no further codable content is correctly, by design, predication — 5D is categorically neutral on modal force (§7); this is not an enum gap.

competence_of.definition: An INSTITUTIONAL actor's own task, power, or mandate includes the object act. Restricted to an INSTITUTIONAL body — a supervisory authority, a board, a notified body, a market surveillance authority, the Commission, a Member State, the AI Office — never a regulated private or individual actor (a controller, a processor, a provider, a deployer, a data subject). Decisive test: competence_of applies ONLY when the text CONFERS or ESTABLISHES a task or power on the actor -- 'shall have the task/power to...', 'shall be competent...', 'is responsible for...', or an enumerated list of tasks or powers (a chapeau + lettered items is the typical surface form, e.g. 'each supervisory authority shall ... (a) monitor ... (b) promote ...'). An institution EXERCISING an already-granted power in a SPECIFIC clause ('shall exercise its powers...', 'may request...', 'shall adopt...') is performs -- exercising a power is a different act from the text that conferred it. 'Responsible for' counts as conferral ONLY in a clause that ASSIGNS the responsibility -- a finite 'is/are responsible for' main verb, with the institutional actor as its own grammatical subject -- never in a REDUCED RELATIVE that merely IDENTIFIES the actor ('...authorities responsible for the enforcement of...', modifying 'authorities' inside a different clause's own object); such a relative stays INSIDE the maximal NP (see spec/SPEC.md's own Unitisation rules), never a separate competence_of Statement. A power, like a right, is a NORMATIVE POSITION (a competence) -- never an endpoint, CONFERRED or not: use this predicate ONLY when the text CONFERS the power itself (the decisive test above); where the text merely DESCRIBES an existing power (naming it, qualifying its exercise), code the act it covers as performs instead. An act's own HOLDER is inherited only from a chapeau or a subject named WITHIN THE SAME UNIT -- never imported from a different unit (see spec/SPEC.md's own Unitisation rules).

performs.definition: An actor performs an act — the non-deontic relation that remains once a modal is stripped from a clause naming any actor OTHER than an institutional body acting under its own mandate ('the controller shall document the assessment' becomes controller performs document_the_assessment; the modal force itself is nD, never part of this Statement). This is also the correct predicate for an INSTITUTIONAL actor EXERCISING an already-granted power in a specific clause ('shall exercise its powers...', 'may request...') -- only CONFERRING or ESTABLISHING a task or power is competence_of (see that predicate's own decisive test); exercising one is performs, the same as any other actor's act. This is ALSO the correct predicate for the ACT a POWER or a RIGHT covers, when the power/right itself is merely DESCRIBED rather than newly conferred: a power, like a right, is a NORMATIVE POSITION (a competence) -- 'power(s) under X' / 'power to X' and 'the right to X' / 'exercise the right to X' are NEVER themselves the object -- the object is the act X names, with the power or right stripped out, the same way a modal is. A Statement id is an invented snake_case label, never a literal copy of the span text -- it MAY add a light verb (e.g. 'seek_X' for an object span naming only 'X') to read as an act, where this predicate needs one.

addressed_to.definition: NEW IN v3.6. The RECIPIENT of an act or communication, as its OWN endpoint -- subj is the act or communication (or the bearer's own action node, e.g. the same act a companion performs/competence_of/requires Statement already names), obj is the party the act runs TO. Cue: a notify/report/inform/communicate/submit/transmit verb (any inflection) followed by its own recipient, either as a direct object ('notify the controller', 'inform the law enforcement or judicial authorities') or via an explicit 'to' ('notify ... to the supervisory authority', 'communicate ... to the data subject', 'report ... to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where...'). The recipient NP is NEVER a bare infinitive or scope phrase riding the SAME word 'to' ('to the extent that', 'to ensure', 'in relation to', 'to be') -- those are not this predicate, and do not even reach the cue test, since the candidate NP must itself read as a recipient (one of the closed ACTOR_ROLES surface forms, or a generic authority/body/Member-State/recipient-shaped NP) before this predicate fires at all. obj is TYPED: the closed ACTOR_ROLES token when the recipient NP's own head matches one of its surface forms (e.g. 'the supervisory authority' -> supervisory_authority, 'the data subject' -> data_subject, 'the controller' -> controller), otherwise the documented other(label) escape (statement.ACTOR_OTHER_RE) -- never silently dropped, and never a bare, untyped copy of the source span. This predicate is layered ON TOP of whatever predicate already claims the HOST clause (performs, competence_of, requires, except_when, ...): it never competes for, and never blocks, that clause's own span -- the SAME clause legitimately carries BOTH 'controller performs notify_the_personal_data_breach' AND 'notify_the_personal_data_breach addressed_to supervisory_authority', from one 'notify ... to ...' cue. negation: "absent" by construction (the SAME R-n reasoning deadline_of already uses: a negator about whether the act happened at all, elsewhere in the host clause, never negates the RELATION naming its own recipient).
